subject.title: fix(agents-bind): generate peer format for feishu group bindings

question: Which public bind grammar should OpenClaw support for Feishu conversation routing while preserving existing account-scoped and channel-only bind behavior?
rationale: The central fix is compatibility-sensitive because current docs define `--bind <channel>:<account>`, while Feishu group routing needs a peer-shaped binding and there are multiple competing open PR shapes.

options.title: Preserve account syntax and add explicit peer support
options.body: Keep existing account/channel resolution intact and add a documented peer grammar or plugin-owned resolver with an explicit account escape and upgrade proof.

options.title: Adopt Feishu two-segment inference
options.body: Treat selected Feishu-looking two-segment values as peers, but require docs, account escape behavior, and proof that existing account names cannot silently misroute.

options.title: Defer and choose a sibling candidate
options.body: Pause this branch and select another open candidate only after it has cleaner compatibility behavior and real proof.

recommendation.title: Preserve account syntax and add explicit peer support
recommendation.body: Keep existing account/channel resolution intact and add a documented peer grammar or plugin-owned resolver with an explicit account escape and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the account-scoped bind command surface being changed, so they are the strongest history-based routing candidate for the grammar decision.
